body:
### Summary

## reproduction
```toml
[project]
name = "repro"
version = "0"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
    "sherpa-onnx-core==1.13.8",
]
[tool.uv]
environments = ["sys_platform == 'android'"]
```
`uv lock` here fails with ``has no `sys_platform == 'android'`-compatible wheels``, even though the package `sherpa-onnx-core` 1.13.8 has wheels for android on arm64_v8a, armeabi_v7a, x86, and x86_64, among other platforms.

## what's happening?
it seems that in #14977, the lockfile wheel filter was given android tag support, but the resolver half wasn't ever created..?
the same PR also added the `lock_android` test, but this has a wheel *with* an sdist, so any kind of platform fork is covered implicitly by the sdist.
and then, in #21672, uv started actually checking environment requirements against forks in packages, which is where this bug started getting  triggered.

## so what's the problem? 
it seems to be that an `android_<api>_<abi>` wheel is not considered `sys_platform == 'android'`, and we missed this because the only locking test for android includes a package with an sdist.

## how'd i find it?
#21672 caused this regression in my specific packaging setup, where there's a marker causing a fork in which package should be used.

after #21672, it throws an error reporting that the package has no compatible wheels, even if they do exist.

to reproduce this secondary bug the same way i did, run `uv lock` on this `pyproject.toml`:
```toml
[project]
name = "repro"
version = "0"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
    "sherpa-onnx-core==1.13.8",
    "certifi==2026.5.20; sys_platform != 'android'",
    "certifi==2026.7.22; sys_platform == 'android'",
]
[tool.uv]
environments = ["python_version >= '3.14'"]
```

running `uv lock` here works fine on uv `0.12.13`, but in `0.12.14` and above (after pr #21672), throws
```
error: No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers: python_full_version >= '3.14' and sys_platform == 'android')
  cause: Because sherpa-onnx-core==1.13.8 has no `python_full_version >= '3.14'`-compatible wheels and your project depends on sherpa-onnx-core==1.13.8, we can conclude that your project's requirements are unsatisfiable.
hint: The resolution failed for an environment that is not the current one, consider limiting the environments with `tool.uv.environments`.
```

## but you don't set `required-environments`, so why is #21672 relevant?
[uv merges `tool.uv.environments` and `required-environments` into a single list.](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/75698b1ed23dd410421de4656304077351641fa7/crates/uv-lock-operations/src/lock.rs#L640)

#21672 changed the check from "does any wheel cover this environment, anywhere in the resolution?" to "does any wheel cover this environment in this specific fork in the resolution"?
so if you don't have any environments entries, it never gets triggered.

the #21672 issue seems to root in that the switch statement in [`implied_platform_markers()` in `uv-resolver`'s `prioritized_distribution.rs`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/1765e51d67f43299d8fbd37b302b773a80c8499d/crates/uv-resolver/src/prioritized_distribution.rs#L1021) does not handle the  `PlatformTag::Android` enum variant.
it just falls through to the "unknown platform tag in wheel tag" debug message, and can end up returning `MarkerTree::FALSE`.



### Platform

Linux 7.2.9 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.13.4 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

3.14.7
title: packages with android wheels but no sdist fail to resolve
